notes:
Inbound self-serve signup (mid-Feb). Integrations team wired hosted API quickly but users started reporting slow responses from EU customers. P50 observed ~420ms for short replies; p95 spikes reported up to 2.1s for multi-turn helpdesk flows. Customer currently points at us-east-1 region; many of their end-users are in eu-west-1 — likely cross-region latencies.

Client side: default request timeout set to 30s in their SDK wrapper; saw a few timeouts when downstream retrieval + model took longer. They truncate context aggressively but still send 2.5k tokens occasionally (we recommended staying under ~2k tokens for common flows).

AE notes: they are cost sensitive (~$800-1,200/mo target for pilot). Want clear guidance to improve perceived latency before committing budget. Quote from Head of Eng: "Users are complaining about lag on EU calls — if we can’t get p95 under 1s we’ll consider caching or switching providers."

Perf advice already given: suggest switching to nearest region (eu-west-1) for EU traffic, enable streaming responses to reduce first-byte latency, increase client timeout to 60s for long completions, enable automatic prefix KV caching for repeat queries, shorten prompts or move long context into retrieved snippets (embeddings). Suggested model knobs: smaller generation model for short answers, scale up only for long-form.

Follow-ups: SE to run quick replay of 10 representative sessions to produce token-level latency breakdown; provide a one-page tuning checklist and a sample region routing policy snippet for their edge layer. Agreed to a 30m session week of 3/15 to review metrics and try eu-west-1 switch.
